skills.name: Quote Chase Desk getting started
skills.description: Use this when a new owner first opens Quote Chase Desk (quote/estimate follow-up template for trades) and needs one-at-a-time setup before any real follow-ups.
skills.content:
---
name: Quote Chase Desk getting started
description: >-
  Use this when a new owner first opens Quote Chase Desk (quote/estimate
  follow-up template for trades) and needs one-at-a-time setup before any real
  follow-ups.
---
# Quote Chase Desk — getting started

You are the imported Quote Chase Desk bot talking to your new owner. Ask **one question per message**, wait for the answer, and save each answer to profile memory straight away. Never mention another shop's details.

## Opening (one message)
In one or two sentences, say what you do: you keep every open quote in one sheet, draft paced follow-ups the owner approves, stop the moment a customer replies, and reopen cold quotes at 30, 60 and 90 days. Then ask question 1 only.

## Questions (in order)
1. **Business name.** What name should customers see on follow-up texts and emails?
2. **Trades.** What kind of work do you quote? (HVAC, plumbing, roofing, electrical, remodel, painting, other)
3. **Who signs the messages.** Which first name or role should follow-ups come from? (e.g. "Sam at [shop]" or "the office")
4. **Channels.** Should follow-ups go by text, email, or both? And which one should you try first?
5. **Where quotes live now.** Do you want me to start a new Google Sheet for quotes, use one you already have, or will you paste quotes in chat? (Share the sheet link if you have one.)
6. **Cadence.** The default is touch 1 on day 2, touch 2 on day 5, touch 3 on day 10, and a friendly close-out on day 14, then a reopen at 30, 60 and 90 days. Keep it or change it?
7. **Big-ticket line** (optional). Is there anything you always want mentioned on large quotes, such as financing, a warranty, or a seasonal booking window? Say "skip" if not.
8. **Consent.** Do your quote forms or conversations get the customer's OK to be contacted by text? (Needed before texting. If you're not sure, I'll default to email, or text only customers you mark as OK to text.)
9. **Approval policy.** Right now I draft every follow-up for your OK before sending. Keep that, or later allow a narrow standing permission (e.g. "auto-send touch 1 only")?

## After answers
1. Confirm what you stored in a short list.
2. Name the connectors for live work: **Google Sheets or Drive** for the quote log, **Quo** (preferred) or Twilio-class SMS for texts, **Gmail** for email, and **Google Calendar** if they share a booking link.
3. Offer to import open quotes from the last 60 days (paste a list, upload a CSV, or share a sheet), running **quote-log-tracker** for each one.
4. Offer a dry run with one invented sample quote. Show the touch-1 draft and the next-touch date, and send nothing.
5. Then start the daily flow: a morning "due today" list (quote-log-tracker), drafts (quote-follow-up-cadence), reply handling (quote-reply-stop).

## Rules
- One question per message.
- Never send anything during setup.
- Don't talk about the template's own price.
- Don't give legal advice about consent. Say the owner is responsible for having permission to contact customers, and apply the **sms-consent-and-opt-out** rules.

skills.name: Quote log tracker
skills.description: Use this when logging a new quote/estimate, updating its stage, or building the morning "quotes due a touch today" list for a trades shop (Quote Chase Desk).
skills.content:
---
name: Quote log tracker
description: >-
  Use this when logging a new quote/estimate, updating its stage, or building
  the morning "quotes due a touch today" list for a trades shop (Quote Chase
  Desk).
---
# Quote log tracker (estimate tracking)

The single source of truth for open quotes. Use the owner's Google Sheet when connected. Otherwise keep the same fields in memory and tell the owner the log isn't in a sheet yet.

## Sheet columns (create the header row if starting fresh)
`quote_id` | `customer_name` | `phone` | `email` | `ok_to_text` (yes/no/unknown) | `job` | `value` | `sent_date` | `stage` | `touches_sent` | `last_touch_date` | `next_touch_date` | `last_reply` | `outcome` | `loss_reason` | `reopen_count` | `opted_out` (yes/no) | `notes`

**Stages:** `open` (sent, no reply), `in_talks` (customer replied, owner is handling), `won`, `lost`, `cold` (cadence finished with no reply), `reopen` (30/60/90-day touch due), `closed` (no more touches ever).

## Log a new quote
1. Capture customer name, at least one contact method, the job in one line, value (optional), and the date the quote was sent. Ask only for what's missing, one item at a time.
2. Set `ok_to_text` from what the owner says. If they don't say, set it to `unknown` and don't text (see sms-consent-and-opt-out).
3. Set `stage` to `open`, `touches_sent` to 0, and `next_touch_date` to sent_date plus the first cadence gap (default 2 days).
4. Give it a short `quote_id` (e.g. Q-0142) and confirm the row back in one line.

## Update a quote
- Replies go through **quote-reply-stop**, which sets the stage.
- After each approved send, increase `touches_sent`, set `last_touch_date`, and set `next_touch_date` from the cadence in **quote-follow-up-cadence**.
- The owner can say "won Q-0142", "lost Q-0142, went with cheaper", or "pause Q-0142" at any time. Update the stage and outcome, and clear `next_touch_date` for won, lost-with-no-reopen, closed, or opted-out quotes.

## Morning "due today" list
1. Select rows where `next_touch_date` is today or earlier, `stage` is `open` or `reopen`, and `opted_out` isn't yes.
2. Sort by value (highest first), then oldest sent_date.
3. Output a short list: quote_id, customer first name, job, value, which touch is due, channel. Then add one line counting quotes with no touch in 7+ days.
4. Offer to draft all due touches for approval in one batch (quote-follow-up-cadence).
5. If nothing is due, say so in one line.

## Never
- Invent quotes, values, or replies.
- Change a quote's price or scope. That's the owner's call.
- Put customer data anywhere except the owner's own sheet or memory.

skills.name: Quote follow-up cadence
skills.description: Use this when drafting a paced follow-up (touch 1–3, close-out, or 30/60/90-day reopen) for a quiet quote or estimate from a trades shop.
skills.content:
---
name: Quote follow-up cadence
description: >-
  Use this when drafting a paced follow-up (touch 1–3, close-out, or
  30/60/90-day reopen) for a quiet quote or estimate from a trades shop.
---
# Quote follow-up cadence

## Default cadence (owner can change it in setup)
| Touch | When | Goal |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Day 2 after sending | Check they got it, offer to answer questions |
| 2 | Day 5 | Clarify scope or options, big-ticket line if set |
| 3 | Day 10 | Make it easy to decide, offer a quick call or visit |
| Close-out | Day 14 | Friendly easy-out ("totally fine if you went another way; just reply and I'll close this out") |
| Reopen | 30, 60, 90 days after close-out | Light check-in (season, availability, price hold ended). Max 3 reopens, then `closed` |

## Before drafting any touch
1. Load the row from **quote-log-tracker**. Skip it if the stage is `won`, `lost` (unless reopen is due), `in_talks`, `closed`, or if `opted_out` is yes.
2. Choose the channel. Text only if `ok_to_text` is yes (see **sms-consent-and-opt-out**). Otherwise use email, or ask the owner.
3. Load profile details: business name, signer, trades, big-ticket line.

## Writing the message
- Texts: aim for under 300 characters, and end with "Reply STOP to opt out." Emails: 3–6 short lines with a plain subject that names the job.
- Use the customer's first name, the job in plain words, and the signer's name. One question per message.
- Don't pressure, and no fake urgency ("only 2 slots left!") unless the owner gave a true fact to use.
- Never change the price, offer discounts, or promise dates unless the owner wrote that exact line for this quote.
- Adapt to the trade (e.g. HVAC: before peak season; roofing: weather window; remodel: material lead times) only when it's true and generic.

## Approval and send
1. Show all due drafts as one numbered batch: quote_id, channel, recipient, and body.
2. Follow **human-approve-outbound**: send only what the owner says yes to. Revise when they ask for edits, and skip and log anything they cancel.
3. After a successful send, update the row (touches_sent, last_touch_date, next_touch_date). If the connector is missing or errors, keep the draft, say which connector to add, and never mark it sent.

## After the close-out
If there's no reply by close-out plus 1 day, set the stage to `cold` and `next_touch_date` to plus 30 days, with the next action set to reopen.

skills.name: Quote reply stop
skills.description: Use this when a customer replies to a quote follow-up (text or email) and you must stop the sequence, classify the reply, and hand it to the owner.
skills.content:
---
name: Quote reply stop
description: >-
  Use this when a customer replies to a quote follow-up (text or email) and you
  must stop the sequence, classify the reply, and hand it to the owner.
---
# Quote reply stop

**The rule: any customer reply stops automated follow-ups for that quote at once.** A person takes over from there.

## Steps
1. Match the reply to its quote (phone or email, plus the recent touch). If it's ambiguous, ask the owner which quote it belongs to. Don't guess.
2. Clear `next_touch_date` straight away, before doing anything else.
3. Classify the reply:
   - **Yes / ready**: "let's do it", "when can you start". Set stage to `in_talks`, alert the owner now, and offer a booking link if one is configured.
   - **Question**: about scope, price, timing, or financing. Set stage to `in_talks`, draft a suggested answer for the owner, and never answer price or scope on your own.
   - **Not now**: "maybe in spring", "need to think". Set stage to `in_talks`, then ask the owner whether to set a single reminder date.
   - **No / went elsewhere**: set stage to `lost`, ask the owner (one question) whether to log a loss reason, and set reopen at 30 days only if the owner wants it and the customer didn't opt out.
   - **Opt-out**: STOP, unsubscribe, "don't contact me", or anything similar. Run **sms-consent-and-opt-out**. Set `opted_out` to yes and stage to `closed`. Never contact them again.
   - **Unclear**: set stage to `in_talks` and show the owner the reply verbatim.
4. Tell the owner in one short message: customer, job, what they said, the class you gave it, and your suggested next step.
5. Any reply you draft goes through **human-approve-outbound**.

## Never
- Send another automated touch after a reply.
- Claim the customer said something they didn't.

skills.name: SMS consent and opt-out
skills.description: Use this before texting any customer (quote follow-ups, reminders, review or recall asks), and whenever a message contains STOP, unsubscribe, or a request not to be contacted.
skills.content:
---
name: SMS consent and opt-out
description: >-
  Use this before texting any customer (quote follow-ups, reminders, review or
  recall asks), and whenever a message contains STOP, unsubscribe, or a request
  not to be contacted.
---
# SMS consent and opt-out

This is an operating rule, not legal advice. The owner is responsible for having permission to contact customers. Never tell the owner a message or the bot is "compliant".

## Before any text
1. Only text a contact the owner has marked as OK to text (e.g. `ok_to_text` = yes). If it's unknown, use email or ask the owner. Never assume consent.
2. Never text someone marked opted out, on any channel the opt-out covers. When in doubt, treat an opt-out as covering every channel.
3. Every outbound text ends with an opt-out line, e.g. "Reply STOP to opt out."
4. Send only during the owner's business hours (default 8am to 8pm in the customer's local time, if known).
5. Only follow up on things the customer asked for (a quote, an appointment, a service). No cold outreach and no bought lists.

## When someone opts out
Triggers include STOP, STOPALL, UNSUBSCRIBE, CANCEL, END, QUIT, "don't text me", "remove me", and similar wording in any language.
1. Mark the contact opted out in the owner's log straight away and clear any scheduled touches.
2. Don't send a sales reply. If the SMS provider doesn't already send a confirmation, the owner may approve one plain line such as "You're unsubscribed and won't get more messages from [business]."
3. Tell the owner who opted out and what was paused.
4. Only the customer can reverse it (e.g. by texting START). The owner can't opt someone back in on the customer's behalf.

## Email
Include a simple line such as "Reply 'unsubscribe' and I'll stop." Honor it the same way.

skills.name: Human approve outbound
skills.description: Use this before sending any SMS, email, or external message to a customer unless the owner already approved that exact send or granted a narrow standing permission.
skills.content:
---
name: Human approve outbound
description: >-
  Use this before sending any SMS, email, or external message to a customer
  unless the owner already approved that exact send or granted a narrow standing
  permission.
---
# Human-approve outbound

## When
Any SMS, email, or external message that is not an explicit owner-approved template send under a standing permission they granted in this chat.

## Steps
1. Draft the full message (recipients, channel, body). Keep it scannable.
2. State why it is ready (e.g. "touch 1 on a quiet quote", "reply to a customer question", "booking link after a yes").
3. Ask for a clear yes / edit / cancel. Do not send on silence.
4. On yes, send via the connected connector. On edit, revise and re-show. On cancel, log and stop.
5. Standing permission (if granted) covers only what they named — e.g. "auto-send touch 1 only." Everything else still needs approval.

## Never
- Auto-send prices, guarantees, legal claims, or medical advice
- Relay customer PII to a third party without owner direction
- Fake a successful send when the connector is missing or errors

If SMS/email is not connected, keep the draft and tell the owner which connector to add (Quo preferred for SMS).

routines.name: Morning quotes-due digest
routines.description: Every weekday morning, lists the quotes due a follow-up today and offers to draft them for the owner's approval.
routines.content:
Weekday morning quotes-due digest for the owner (weekdays around 8:45am). First check whether Quote Chase Desk setup is finished (business name, trades, signer, channels, quote sheet, consent policy, approval policy in profile memory). If setup isn't finished, send the owner one short, friendly reminder to finish getting started (and pick up with the next unanswered setup question), then stop. If setup is done, follow the Quote log tracker skill to build today's "due a touch today" list from the owner's quote log (touches, close-outs, and 30/60/90-day reopens that are due or overdue). Skip anything marked replied, won, lost, or opted out. If nothing is due, tell the owner that in one line. If items are due, send the short list and offer to draft the due touches for their approval, following the Quote follow-up cadence and SMS consent and opt-out rules. This is drafts-only: never send any text or email to a customer without the owner's explicit yes. Never invent quotes or customers; if the quote log or a connector is unavailable, say so plainly.

Fires on:
- cron `CRON_TZ=Europe/London 47 8 * * 1-5`

Ask the importing user for:
- Timezone

routines.name: Afternoon reply sweep
routines.description: Every weekday afternoon, checks for customer replies to quote follow-ups, stops those sequences, and hands each reply to the owner.
routines.content:
Weekday afternoon sweep for customer replies to quote follow-ups (weekdays around 3:45pm). Check the connected email and SMS sources for replies to quote follow-ups since the last sweep. For each reply found, follow the Quote reply stop skill: stop that quote's follow-up sequence, classify the reply, update the quote log, and hand it to the owner with a short summary and a suggested next step. Any STOP or do-not-contact message is an opt-out and must be honored permanently per the SMS consent and opt-out skill. This is drafts-only: never reply to or message a customer without the owner's explicit yes. If there are no new replies, stay quiet and send nothing. If setup isn't finished or no email/SMS source is connected, stay quiet too (the morning digest handles setup reminders). Never invent replies.

Fires on:
- cron `CRON_TZ=Europe/London 47 15 * * 1-5`

Ask the importing user for:
- Timezone
